title: How Kensington Colonials Load Connecticut Avenue Pollen Into Ducts
headline: Antique Row weekends, Howard Avenue brick, and why basement trunks sweat in close-in Montgomery
description: Kensington, MD colonials sit on Connecticut Avenue under street trees. Learn why pollen and weekend grit load cool basement ducts, and when to clean them from Bethesda.

sections.heading: Connecticut Avenue is a pollen and grit corridor
paragraphs: Kensington sits between Bethesda and Wheaton: Antique Row on Howard Avenue, Connecticut Avenue through the middle, then Kensington Heights toward Silver Spring. Early- and mid-century colonials have full basements. Those rooms stay cool. Oak and maple on the avenue dump debris onto every stoop. Returns pull it in. Weekend traffic from Antique Row adds a finer grit that a quiet cul-de-sac never sees.
When humid air hits cold supply trunks, that film turns the first AC cycle into a dust event you can see on the registers.

sections.heading: The basement air handler is storing last April
paragraphs: It cools the colonial. It also sits in the dampest room. Cold trunks sweat. Street-tree pollen is already inside. Together they are what mold needs. A second-floor laundry often sends lint on a long drop to a rear wall.
If wiping the registers only lasts a few days, start with [air duct cleaning in Kensington, MD](/locations/kensington).

sections.heading: Typical signs in a Kensington colonial
listItems: Yellow-gray film on upstairs supplies during peak pollen.
Musty basement air when the AC starts after a humid week.
Dust returning fast on Connecticut Avenue or Howard Avenue sides of the house.

sections.heading: Up Connecticut from Bethesda — not an Antique Row suite
paragraphs: Kensington is served from our [Bethesda](/locations/bethesda) office. Nearby [Wheaton](/locations/wheaton) and [Silver Spring](/locations/silver-spring) use the same dispatch. There is no Kensington storefront.
Book on the [Kensington location page](/locations/kensington). See [air duct cleaning](/air-duct-cleaning) for what we pull out of those basement trunks.
listItems: Change filters when Connecticut Avenue trees are dumping pollen.
Keep basement humidity under 50% in summer.
Clean ducts every 3 to 5 years; clear dryer vents about once a year.

faq.q: Does Connecticut Avenue pollen really end up in Kensington ducts?
faq.a: Yes. Returns pull outdoor air and whatever settled on the stoop. Heavy spring pollen shows up as film on registers until the system is cleaned.

faq.a: No. Kensington is served from Bethesda. We will not rent a Howard Avenue mailbox and call it an office.
